title: `nudgeSize == 1` is a footgun: any single-mint batchMint qualifies as 'batch' and drains nudge pool
economicDescription:
`setNudgeSize` accepts any `uint256` value with no minimum. The check at line 139 is `count >= _nudgeSize`. If the owner ever sets `nudgeSize = 1`, every `batchMint(count=1, ...)` qualifies for the nudge — including any single-mint call. The contract is named 'BatchNFTMinter' but does not actually enforce a true batch (`count > 1`). The storage slot defaults to 0 (which disables, per the comment), so an owner mistakenly typing 1 instead of e.g. 10 would convert any single mint into a nudge claim, defeating the design. Combined with ECON-001/003, this means a fat-finger by the owner is immediately and permanently exploitable until rectified.

Similarly, the contract does not enforce `nudgeSize <= some_reasonable_max`, so a typo of e.g. `nudgeSize = 10**18` would silently disable the feature in practice (no batch will ever reach that size) without emitting a warning or revert. Less harmful but still a footgun.
attackScenario:
1. Owner intends nudgeSize=10 but submits tx with arg=1 (typo / wrong decimal interpretation / off-by-one in deployment script).
2. Tx succeeds; emits NudgeSizeChanged(1).
3. ANY user (or attacker bot) calling batchMint(count=1, recipient, ...) drains the entire nudge pool on the first call.
4. Continues every refill cycle.
profitability: Same as ECON-001 but with even lower mint cost (single mint).
recommendedMitigation: Add `require(newSize >= 2, ...)` in `setNudgeSize` to enforce that 'batch' means at least 2 mints. Alternatively, document a reasonable minimum (e.g. 5) and warn off-chain. A `MIN_NUDGE_SIZE` constant analogous to `MAX_TARGET_APY` in NFTStaker would make the bound explicit and on-chain.
intentReference: Comment line 19-22 says 'when count >= nudgeSize and nudgePaymentToken is set ... transfers ...'. No documented minimum. NFTStaker has analogous bounds (MAX_TARGET_APY) — the asymmetry is the finding.
